correctness.rationale: PASS: In R_{m,n} a currently blue rook cell (i,j) has exactly degree_H(row_i)+degree_H(col_j) white neighbors. Existence of a first move iff an isolate on one side and degree-one opposite side. Any white bipartite cycle cannot have its first edge forced, so success requires acyclic H. After the first leaf force a row and column are isolated, and every remaining nonempty forest has a leaf which can be paired with opposite isolate; induction forces all white edges. Component EGF correctly uses p^(q-1)q^(p-1) bipartite trees and surjective-word Stirling counts of no-row/no-column-leaf cases. Two-sort exponential formula counts all eligible forests. Minimum sets arise from one isolate plus a spanning tree with an opposite-color leaf, yielding the stated Stirling expression; m=n=1 and min(m,n)=1 treated separately. Independent direct ZF simulation matches forest criterion for 1x1,2x3,3x3,4x4 (65,536 colorings at 4x4), including polynomial white-edge profiles.
